title: Preserve the real proof boundary in SMOKE tests

facts.note: Primary activation: any test file whose declared Phase is SMOKE, whether or not it currently contains substitution. Requires an observer that reads the file's declared Phase (bun_tester_discipline_detector already parses it); no filename convention is assumed.
Any file that declares a test Phase, recognised by the Phase declaration itself rather than by a filename pattern.
Bun test stack (bun:test, plus jest/vitest substitution vocabulary).

fires: The tester creates or edits any case in a test file declaring Phase SMOKE, including a currently compliant one.
A SMOKE-phase test calls mock.module, spyOn, jest.mock/spyOn or vi.mock/spyOn on a production collaborator.
A test using mocks or spies is being relabeled as SMOKE.
doesNotFire: A UNIT-phase test file uses mock.module or spyOn.
Non-test source files with no declared test Phase.

given: A test file whose declared Phase is SMOKE
when: the tester writes or edits a case in that file
then: Preserve the real proof boundary: the case MUST exercise the production collaborator through the assembled path the SMOKE acceptance requires, on the real infrastructure or environment the declared smoke proof verifies, and MUST NOT substitute any production collaborator (mock.module, spyOn, jest.mock/spyOn, vi.mock/spyOn).
prefer: Arrange only the minimum preconditions needed for the declared stimulus.
Observe the acceptance-specific external result after the real collaborator runs.
If substitution is the intended proof technique, move the case into a UNIT-phase test where it is honest and expected.
avoid: Replacing the collaborator the SMOKE claim depends on because it is expensive, inconvenient or hard to arrange — that changes the question, not the cost.
Moving the test inward to a unit seam merely because it is easier to control.
Relabeling a case as SMOKE after using mocks or spies that bypass production behavior.
unless: The file is not SMOKE-phase: UNIT tests may substitute freely.
why: In a SMOKE proof the boundary is part of the claim: a substituted SMOKE test (perhaps a fine unit test) earns gate credit for the very path it replaced, letting a green suite coexist with a broken deployment.
evidence: bun_tester_discipline_detector reports no substitution call in any SMOKE-phase file (each finding reports the exact line).
The case would fail if the real collaborator or production wiring were broken.
The observable assertion proves the bound acceptance rather than the test fixture.
verifier_detail: Detector: bun_tester_discipline_detector (type validator). Scope: only files whose Phase is SMOKE are scanned; UNIT-phase files are not.
Term 'substitution': mock.module, spyOn, jest.mock/spyOn, vi.mock/spyOn — replacing a production collaborator. bun:test exposes mock and spyOn where pytest uses monkeypatch.
Flags any substitution call in a SMOKE-phase file, reporting the exact line. A substitution finding is violation evidence, not an activation prerequisite.
Term 'false_evidence': what a substituted SMOKE test gives the gate — credit that the real path works, when the real path is precisely what was replaced.

Substituting a collaborator turns a SMOKE test into a unit test wearing a SMOKE label; the damage is not that the test is bad (it may be an excellent unit test) but that the gate counts it as evidence the real path works. This is the failure ATDD's phase separation exists to prevent.

sharedNodes.text: Strict disposition: fails on every finding; no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.
